body:
## Updated 2026-10-31: owner target for Mark II

**Target:** the routed Mark II image uses **fewer than 20,000 LUTs** (about 31.5 % of `xc7a100t`), at **32x32 streams**: 16x16 logical streams, each redundant on both networks, on the single TDM8 bus. This replaces the 60 % (38,040-LUT) target below; NFR-RES-01 in `docs/reference/FR_NFR.md` is amended to match.

**Owner decisions (2026-10-31):**
- **The protocol processor is removed** (16:33). ADP, ACMP, MAAP, SRP, AECP and saved-state handling become CPU software only (#665). No fabric processor stays in the end state.
- **gPTP moves to software** (16:51, 17:04): the `flexptpd` implementation, the one the test machine runs. Hardware timestamping stays in fabric on both ports.
- **`milan_csr` stays, for information and diagnostics only.** The diagnostics stay in fabric and are read through it (D2).
- **milan_dp keeps only the crossbar and the stream endpoints:** channel maps, TDM capture and render, and AVTP/AAF packetizing and depacketizing. The media clock and the MAC/time plane sit beside it. The frame filtering (TCAM) stays.
- **Talker latency:** as fast as possible, ideally **below 65 µs** for every talker stream. It is measured from the last sample of a packet at the TDM pin to the frame's first bit on the wire.
- **LiteX is removed, in stages** (17:21), **and the image goes as low as possible**: below 20,000 LUTs is the ceiling, not the goal. The stages are: drop DDR3 and the BIOS ROM; replace LiteEth and LiteSPI with proven AXI cores; then a plain SystemVerilog top replaces the SoC generator.
- **Start:** right after the current release tasks (the merge train and the qualification pre-run).

**Estimate** (the 1x1 shipping image after placement, 52,008 LUTs, minus the processor, plus the measured split CPU and mailbox): about 34.2k LUTs. Levers, least risky first (cumulative, central):

| # | Lever | Risk | LUT saved | Cumulative |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|
| 1 | Drop DDR3, on-chip main memory (D4) | low | ~1.0k | ~33.2k |
| 2 | Slimmer LiteX bus and CSR banks | low-medium | ~1.0k | ~32.2k |
| 3 | `milan_csr` reduced to information and diagnostics | medium | ~1.75k | ~30.5k |
| 4 | One CPU (no second hart) | high | ~3.55k | ~26.9k |
| 5 | MMCM servo in firmware | high | ~1.0k | ~25.9k |
| 6 | gPTP to software (decided) | very high | ~5.2k | ~20.7k |

Central figures stop just above 20k, so the retained-table and width levers (L3/L4 in `docs/design/MARK_II_AREA_PLAN.md`) and the LiteX FIFO trims are also needed.

**What 32x32 requires** (#819 measured +1,514 fabric LUTs per stream pair outside the processor; replicated to 32 pairs that is ~47k):
- **Time-multiplexed stream engines.** One packetizer and one depacketizer serve every stream, with per-stream contexts in Block RAM.
- **Audio buffers bounded by the TDM8 bus.** One talker capture buffer sized by the packet interval, and one 8-slot listener render buffer sized by the presentation time offset. Neither grows with the stream count.
- **Packet boundaries staggered over the six sample phases** of the 125 µs class-A interval, so the class-A shaper does not hold the last stream past the 65 µs target.
- **Redundancy:** a second MAC, filter and timestamp port.
- **Block RAM** budgeted with the LUTs: firmware state for 64 streams, per-stream contexts and the LiteX FIFOs (today 29 + 18 RAMB36).

**Acceptance (2026-10-31):**
- The routed Mark II image at 32x32 uses fewer than 20,000 LUTs, fits the Block RAM, and meets the build's timing gate at every corner.
- Every talker stream meets the 65 µs target, measured on the bench.
- Function is unchanged: every suite, campaign and compliance check passes; the gPTP qualification passes on the software implementation.
- The resource gate's baseline is re-recorded in the reviewed change that reaches the target.

Plan and measurements: comments of 2026-10-31 on this issue.

---

## Original text (2026-10-03)

**Owner decision (2026-10-03):** NFR-RES-01 stays at 60 %. It will be met by a redesign once every other milestone is reached, under this milestone.

**Starting point** (issue #234 baseline, PR #638, `docs/findings/234_PP_SHADOW_AREA_BASELINE.md`):
- The routed shipping image uses 50,128 LUTs, 79.07 % of `xc7a100t`. That is 12,088 LUTs over the 38,040-LUT target (NFR-RES-01 in `docs/reference/FR_NFR.md`).
- `KL_pp_shadow` alone uses 24,343 LUTs in its 1x1 standalone synthesis.
- The ranked levers (#232, #230, #639) recover about 3,600 LUTs. #233 alone cannot close the gap.

**Until then:** the resource gate (PR #638) holds every resource at its recorded value, so the image cannot grow unreviewed.

**Acceptance:**
- The routed shipping image uses at most 38,040 LUTs and meets the build's timing gate at the shipping clock.
- Function is unchanged: every suite, campaign and compliance check passes at the same counts.
- The resource gate's baseline is re-recorded in the reviewed change that reaches the target.

Relates to #229.
title: [Optimisation] Mark II: below 20,000 LUTs at 32x32 (16x16 redundant) by redesign
